title: AlpineFit's shrinking margin
prompt: AlpineFit operates 18 premium fitness clubs across the Mountain West. Revenue grew 8% last year, yet EBITDA margin fell from 19% to 13%. Management wants to understand the primary driver and choose a practical response before the next planning cycle.
objective: Identify the primary cause of AlpineFit's EBITDA-margin decline and recommend a practical response that protects the member experience.

clarificationOptions.label: Which performance metric should we explain?
clarificationOptions.response: Focus on the six-point decline in EBITDA margin, not absolute revenue growth.

clarificationOptions.label: Over what period did performance change?
clarificationOptions.response: Compare the most recent twelve months with the prior twelve months.

clarificationOptions.label: Is the issue concentrated in a product or geography?
clarificationOptions.response: All 18 clubs are in scope, though the decline varies meaningfully by location.

clarificationOptions.label: Have competitors changed prices?
clarificationOptions.response: Competitor pricing has been broadly stable and is not management's immediate concern.

facts.text: Revenue grew 8%, led by member volume rather than price.
Average membership price was effectively flat year over year.
Operating costs grew 17%, substantially faster than revenue.
Fixed occupancy and corporate costs grew 3%, below revenue growth.
Variable operating costs grew 28% and explain most of the margin decline.
Club labor expense grew 34%, while staffed service hours grew only 11%.
Cleaning supplies and member amenities rose in line with visits.
Overtime hours nearly tripled, with the highest usage in six clubs.
Open trainer and front-desk roles have remained unfilled for an average of 74 days.
The six high-overtime clubs have 31% annual staff turnover versus 12% elsewhere.
Current overtime creates approximately $756,000 of incremental annual labor expense.

investigationNodes.label: Understand revenue performance
investigationNodes.interviewerResponse: Revenue is not declining; it grew 8%, mostly from more members.

investigationNodes.label: Check membership pricing
investigationNodes.interviewerResponse: Average membership price was essentially unchanged.

investigationNodes.label: Check member volume
investigationNodes.interviewerResponse: Membership increased 9%, so volume is a tailwind rather than the problem.

investigationNodes.label: Break down operating costs
investigationNodes.interviewerResponse: Operating costs grew 17%. The cost-category exhibit is now available.

investigationNodes.label: Inspect fixed costs
investigationNodes.interviewerResponse: Fixed costs grew more slowly than revenue and do not explain the decline.

investigationNodes.label: Inspect variable costs
investigationNodes.interviewerResponse: Variable operating costs grew 28% and warrant a deeper breakdown.

investigationNodes.label: Inspect club labor
investigationNodes.interviewerResponse: Labor expense grew far faster than staffed hours. Overtime and vacancies can be investigated next.

investigationNodes.label: Inspect supplies and amenities
investigationNodes.interviewerResponse: These costs rose in line with club visits and are not driving the margin decline.

investigationNodes.label: Inspect overtime usage
investigationNodes.interviewerResponse: Overtime nearly tripled and is concentrated in six clubs. The location exhibit is now available.

investigationNodes.label: Inspect open roles
investigationNodes.interviewerResponse: Key club roles have remained open for an average of 74 days.

investigationNodes.label: Compare staff turnover
investigationNodes.interviewerResponse: High-overtime clubs also have much higher turnover, creating a self-reinforcing staffing gap.

insights.label: Labor accounts for most of the cost increase.
Every cost category rose at the same rate.

exhibits.title: Overtime and staff turnover by club group

insights.label: High overtime and high turnover occur in the same six clubs.
The issue is evenly distributed across all clubs.

calculations.prompt: The six affected clubs each use 3,600 annual overtime hours, and the overtime premium is $35 per hour. What is the total incremental annual expense?

decisions.label: Stabilize staffing in the six affected clubs with targeted retention and faster hiring while tightening overtime controls.
Raise membership prices across every club immediately.
Reduce member amenities across the network.

risks.label: Retention incentives may not reduce turnover quickly enough.
Reducing overtime too quickly could disrupt club service.
Broad price increases could trigger member churn.

nextSteps.label: Run a 90-day staffing pilot in the six high-overtime clubs.
Raise prices in all 18 clubs next month.

efficientPaths.label: Cost growth to staffing root cause
Confirm the revenue trend, then isolate labor
